http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Resistance (real part of impedance).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCConverterDCTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A DC electrical connection point at the AC/DC converter. The AC/DC converter is electrically connected also to the AC side. The AC connection is inherited from the AC conducting equipment in the same way as any other AC equipment. The AC/DC converter DC terminal is separate from generic DC terminal to restrict the connection with the AC side to AC/DC converter and so that no other DC conducting equipment can be connected to the AC side.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCPolarityKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Polarity for DC circuits.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CsConverter
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: DC side of the current source converter (CSC).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AngleDegrees
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Measurement of angle in degrees.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CurrentFlow
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Electrical current with sign convention: positive flow is out of the conducting equipment into the connectivity node. Can be both AC and DC.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCBaseTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electrical connection point at a piece of DC conducting equipment. DC terminals are connected at one physical DC node that may have multiple DC terminals connected. A DC node is similar to an AC connectivity node. The model enforces that DC connections are distinct from AC connections.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCBreaker
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A breaker within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCBusbar
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A busbar within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCChopper
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Low resistance equipment used in the internal DC circuit to balance voltages. It has typically positive and negative pole terminals and a ground.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCConductingEquipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The parts of the DC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through DC terminals.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCConverterOperatingModeKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The operating mode of an HVDC bipole.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCConverterUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Indivisible operative unit comprising all equipment between the point of common coupling on the AC side and the point of common coupling – DC side, essentially one or more converters, together with one or more converter transformers, converter control equipment, essential protective and switching devices and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCDisconnector
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A disconnector within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCEquipmentContainer
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A modeling construct to provide a root class for containment of DC as well as AC equipment. The class differ from the EquipmentContaner for AC in that it may also contain DCNodes. Hence it can contain both AC and DC equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCGround
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A ground within a DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Inductance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Inductive part of reactance (imaginary part of impedance), at rated frequency.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCLine
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Overhead lines and/or cables connecting two or more HVDC substations.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCLineSegment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A wire or combination of wires not insulated from one another, with consistent electrical characteristics, used to carry direct current between points in the DC region of the power system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Capacitance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Capacitive part of reactance (imaginary part of impedance), at rated frequency.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Length
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Unit of length. Never negative.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCNode
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: DC nodes are points where terminals of DC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCSeriesDevice
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A series device within the DC system, typically a reactor used for filtering or smoothing.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCShunt
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A shunt device within the DC system, typically used for filtering.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCSwitch
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A switch within the DC system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electrical connection point to generic DC conducting equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CapacitancePerLength
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Capacitance per unit of length.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: InductancePerLength
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Inductance per unit of length.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ResistancePerLength
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Resistance (real part of impedance) per unit of length.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: VsCapabilityCurve
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The P-Q capability curve for a voltage source converter, with P on x-axis and Qmin and Qmax on y1-axis and y2-axis.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: VsConverter
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: DC side of the voltage source converter (VSC).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Simple_Float
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: BusNameMarker
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Used to apply user standard names to topology buses. Typically used for "bus/branch" case generation. Associated with one or more terminals that are normally connected with the bus name.    The associated terminals are normally connected by non-retained switches. For a ring bus station configuration, all busbar terminals in the ring are typically associated.   For a breaker and a half scheme, both busbars would normally be associated.  For a ring bus, all busbars would normally be associated.  For a "straight" busbar configuration, normally only the main terminal at the busbar would be associated.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Accumulator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Accumulator represents an accumulated (counted) Measurement, e.g. an energy value.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AccumulatorLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Limit values for Accumulator measurements.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AccumulatorLimitSet
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An AccumulatorLimitSet specifies a set of Limits that are associated with an Accumulator measurement.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AccumulatorReset
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: This command reset the counter value to zero.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AccumulatorValue
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: AccumulatorValue represents an accumulated (counted) MeasurementValue.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Analog
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Analog represents an analog Measurement.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Boolean
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AnalogControl
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An analog control used for supervisory control.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AnalogLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Limit values for Analog measurements.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AnalogLimitSet
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An AnalogLimitSet specifies a set of Limits that are associated with an Analog measurement.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AnalogValue
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: AnalogValue represents an analog MeasurementValue.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Command
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A Command is a discrete control used for supervisory control.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Control
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Control is used for supervisory/device control. It represents control outputs that are used to change the state in a process, e.g. close or open breaker, a set point value or a raise lower command.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DateTime
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Discrete
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Discrete represents a discrete Measurement, i.e. a Measurement representing discrete values, e.g. a Breaker position.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DiscreteValue
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: DiscreteValue represents a discrete MeasurementValue.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Limit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Specifies one limit value for a Measurement. A Measurement typically has several limits that are kept together by the LimitSet class. The actual meaning and use of a Limit instance (i.e., if it is an alarm or warning limit or if it is a high or low limit) is not captured in the Limit class. However the name of a Limit instance may indicate both meaning and use.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LimitSet
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Specifies a set of Limits that are associated with a Measurement. A Measurement may have several LimitSets corresponding to seasonal or other changing conditions. The condition is captured in the name and description attributes. The same LimitSet may be used for several Measurements. In particular percentage limits are used this way.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Measurement
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A Measurement represents any measured, calculated or non-measured non-calculated quantity. Any piece of equipment may contain Measurements, e.g. a substation may have temperature measurements and door open indications, a transformer may have oil temperature and tank pressure measurements, a bay may contain a number of power flow measurements and a Breaker may contain a switch status measurement. 
The PSR - Measurement association is intended to capture this use of Measurement and is included in the naming hierarchy based on EquipmentContainer. The naming hierarchy typically has Measurements as leafs, e.g. Substation-VoltageLevel-Bay-Switch-Measurement.
Some Measurements represent quantities related to a particular sensor location in the network, e.g. a voltage transformer (PT) at a busbar or a current transformer (CT) at the bar between a breaker and an isolator. The sensing position is not captured in the PSR - Measurement association. Instead it is captured by the Measurement - Terminal association that is used to define the sensing location in the network topology. The location is defined by the connection of the Terminal to ConductingEquipment. 
If both a Terminal and PSR are associated, and the PSR is of type ConductingEquipment, the associated Terminal should belong to that ConductingEquipment instance.
When the sensor location is needed both Measurement-PSR and Measurement-Terminal are used. The Measurement-Terminal association is never used alone.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseCode
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Enumeration of phase identifiers. Allows designation of phases for both transmission and distribution equipment, circuits and loads.
Residential and small commercial loads are often served from single-phase, or split-phase, secondary circuits. For example of s12N, phases 1 and 2 refer to hot wires that are 180 degrees out of phase, while N refers to the neutral wire. Through single-phase transformer connections, these secondary circuits may be served from one or two of the primary phases A, B, and C. For three-phase loads, use the A, B, C phase codes instead of s12N.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: MeasurementValue
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The current state for a measurement. A state value is an instance of a measurement from a specific source. Measurements can be associated with many state values, each representing a different source for the measurement.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PerCent
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Percentage on a defined base.   For example, specify as 100 to indicate at the defined base.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: MeasurementValueQuality
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Measurement quality flags. Bits 0-10 are defined for substation automation in draft IEC 61850 part 7-3. Bits 11-15 are reserved for future expansion by that document. Bits 16-31 are reserved for EMS applications.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: MeasurementValueSource
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: MeasurementValueSource describes the alternative sources updating a MeasurementValue. User conventions for how to use the MeasurementValueSource attributes are described in the introduction to IEC 61970-301.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Quality61850
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Quality flags in this class are as defined in IEC 61850, except for estimatorReplaced, which has been included in this class for convenience.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Source
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Source gives information related to the origin of a value.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Validity
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Validity for MeasurementValue.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RaiseLowerCommand
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An analog control that increase or decrease a set point value with pulses.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SetPoint
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An analog control that issue a set point value.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: StringMeasurement
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: StringMeasurement represents a measurement with values of type string.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: StringMeasurementValue
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: StringMeasurementValue represents a measurement value of type string.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ValueAliasSet
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes the translation of a set of values into a name and is intendend to facilitate cusom translations. Each ValueAliasSet has a name, description etc. A specific Measurement may represent a discrete state like Open, Closed, Intermediate etc. This requires a translation from the MeasurementValue.value number to a string, e.g. 0->"Invalid", 1->"Open", 2->"Closed", 3->"Intermediate". Each ValueToAlias member in ValueAliasSet.Value describe a mapping for one particular value to a name.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ValueToAlias
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes the translation of one particular value into a name, e.g. 1 as "Open".

http://entsoe.eu/CIM/SchemaExtension/3/1.label: EnergySchedulingType
http://entsoe.eu/CIM/SchemaExtension/3/1.comment: Used to define the type of generation for scheduling purposes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EnergySource
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generic equivalent for an energy supplier on a transmission or distribution voltage level.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AngleRadians
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Phase angle in radians.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Reactance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Reactance (imaginary part of impedance), at rated frequency.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: FossilFuel
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The fossil fuel consumed by the non-nuclear thermal generating unit.   For example, coal, oil, gas, etc.   This a the specific fuels that the generating unit can consume.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: FuelType
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Type of fuel.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A single or set of synchronous machines for converting mechanical power into alternating-current power. For example, individual machines within a set may be defined for scheduling purposes while a single control signal is derived for the set. In this case there would be a GeneratingUnit for each member of the set and an additional GeneratingUnit corresponding to the set.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GeneratorControlSource
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The source of controls for a generating unit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Money
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Amount of money.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Currency
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Monetary currencies. Apologies for this list not being exhaustive.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Decimal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Decimal is the base-10 notational system for representing real numbers.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GrossToNetActivePowerCurve
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Relationship between the generating unit's gross active power output on the X-axis (measured at the terminals of the machine(s)) and the generating unit's net active power output on the Y-axis (based on utility-defined measurements at the power station). Station service loads, when modeled, should be treated as non-conforming bus loads. There may be more than one curve, depending on the auxiliary equipment that is in service.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: HydroEnergyConversionKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Specifies the capability of the hydro generating unit to convert energy as a generator or pump.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: HydroGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generating unit whose prime mover is a hydraulic turbine (e.g., Francis, Pelton, Kaplan).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: HydroPlantStorageKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The type of hydro power plant.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: HydroPowerPlant
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A hydro power station which can generate or pump. When generating, the generator turbines receive water from an upper reservoir. When pumping, the pumps receive their water from a lower reservoir.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: HydroPump
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A synchronous motor-driven pump, typically associated with a pumped storage plant.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: NuclearGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A nuclear generating unit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SolarGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A solar thermal generating unit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ThermalGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generating unit whose prime mover could be a steam turbine, combustion turbine, or diesel engine.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: WindGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A wind driven generating unit.  May be used to represent a single turbine or an aggregation.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: WindGenUnitKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Kind of wind generating unit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electrical connection point (AC or DC) to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: BaseVoltage
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Defines a system base voltage which is referenced.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: BasicIntervalSchedule
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Schedule of values at points in time.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Bay
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A collection of power system resources (within a given substation) including conducting equipment, protection relays, measurements, and telemetry.  A bay typically represents a physical grouping related to modularization of equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConductingEquipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The parts of the AC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through terminals.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConnectivityNode
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Connectivity nodes are points where terminals of AC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConnectivityNodeContainer
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A base class for all objects that may contain connectivity nodes or topological nodes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Curve
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A multi-purpose curve or functional relationship between an independent variable (X-axis) and dependent (Y-axis) variables.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CurveStyle
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Style or shape of curve.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CurveData
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Multi-purpose data points for defining a curve.  The use of this generic class is discouraged if a more specific class  can be used to specify the x and y axis values along with their specific data types.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Equipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The parts of a power system that are physical devices, electronic or mechanical.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EquipmentContainer
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A modeling construct to provide a root class for containing equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GeographicalRegion
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A geographical region of a power system network model.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: IdentifiedObject
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: This is a root class to provide common identification for all classes needing identification and naming attributes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PowerSystemResource
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A power system resource can be an item of equipment such as a switch, an equipment container containing many individual items of equipment such as a substation, or an organisational entity such as sub-control area. Power system resources can have measurements associated.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegularIntervalSchedule
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The schedule has time points where the time between them is constant.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Seconds
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Time, in seconds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegularTimePoint
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Time point for a schedule where the time between the consecutive points is constant.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ReportingGroup
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A reporting group is used for various ad-hoc groupings used for reporting.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SubGeographicalRegion
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A subset of a geographical region of a power system network model.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Substation
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A collection of equipment for purposes other than generation or utilization, through which electric energy in bulk is passed for the purposes of switching or modifying its characteristics.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Terminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An AC electrical connection point to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: VoltageLevel
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A collection of equipment at one common system voltage forming a switchgear. The equipment typically consist of breakers, busbars, instrumentation, control, regulation and protection devices as well as assemblies of all these.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ActivePowerLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Limit on active power flow.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ApparentPowerLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Apparent power limit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CurrentLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Operational limit on current.

http://entsoe.eu/CIM/SchemaExtension/3/1.label: LimitTypeKind
http://entsoe.eu/CIM/SchemaExtension/3/1.comment: The enumeration defines the kinds of the limit types.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: OperationalLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A value associated with a specific kind of limit. 
The sub class value attribute shall be positive. 
The sub class value attribute is inversely proportional to OperationalLimitType.acceptableDuration (acceptableDuration for short). A pair of value_x and acceptableDuration_x are related to each other as follows:
if value_1 > value_2 > value_3 >... then
acceptableDuration_1 < acceptableDuration_2 < acceptableDuration_3 < ...
A value_x with direction="high" shall be greater than a value_y with direction="low".

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: OperationalLimitDirectionKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The direction attribute describes the side of  a limit that is a violation.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: OperationalLimitSet
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A set of limits associated with equipment.  Sets of limits might apply to a specific temperature, or season for example. A set of limits may contain different severities of limit levels that would apply to the same equipment. The set may contain limits of different types such as apparent power and current limits or high and low voltage limits  that are logically applied together as a set.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: OperationalLimitType
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The operational meaning of a category of limits.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: VoltageLimit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Operational limit applied to voltage.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACLineSegment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A wire or combination of wires, with consistent electrical characteristics, building a single electrical system, used to carry alternating current between points in the power system.
For symmetrical, transposed 3ph lines, it is sufficient to use  attributes of the line segment, which describe impedances and admittances for the entire length of the segment.  Additionally impedances can be computed by using length and associated per length impedances.
The BaseVoltage at the two ends of ACLineSegments in a Line shall have the same BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage. However, boundary lines  may have slightly different BaseVoltage.nominalVoltages and  variation is allowed. Larger voltage difference in general requires use of an equivalent branch.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Susceptance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Imaginary part of admittance.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Conductance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Factor by which voltage must be multiplied to give corresponding power lost from a circuit. Real part of admittance.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Temperature
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Value of temperature in degrees Celsius.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AsynchronousMachine
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A rotating machine whose shaft rotates asynchronously with the electrical field.  Also known as an induction machine with no external connection to the rotor windings, e.g squirrel-cage induction machine.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Frequency
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Cycles per second.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RotationSpeed
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Number of revolutions per second.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Breaker
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal circuit conditions and also making, carrying for a specified time, and breaking currents under specified abnormal circuit conditions e.g.  those of short circuit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: BusbarSection
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A conductor, or group of conductors, with negligible impedance, that serve to connect other conducting equipment within a single substation. 
Voltage measurements are typically obtained from VoltageTransformers that are connected to busbar sections. A bus bar section may have many physical terminals but for analysis is modelled with exactly one logical terminal.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Conductor
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Combination of conducting material with consistent electrical characteristics, building a single electrical system, used to carry current between points in the power system.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Connector
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A conductor, or group of conductors, with negligible impedance, that serve to connect other conducting equipment within a single substation and are modelled with a single logical terminal.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Disconnector
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A manually operated or motor operated mechanical switching device used for changing the connections in a circuit, or for isolating a circuit or equipment from a source of power. It is required to open or close circuits when negligible current is broken or made.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EarthFaultCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A conducting equipment used to represent a connection to ground which is typically used to compensate earth faults..   An earth fault compensator device modeled with a single terminal implies a second terminal solidly connected to ground.  If two terminals are modeled, the ground is not assumed and normal connection rules apply.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EnergyConsumer
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Generic user of energy - a  point of consumption on the power system model.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ReactivePower
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the quadrature component of the current.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ExternalNetworkInjection
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: This class represents external network and it is used for IEC 60909 calculations.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ActivePowerPerFrequency
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Active power variation with frequency.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PU
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Per Unit - a positive or negative value referred to a defined base. Values typically range from -10 to +10.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Ground
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A point where the system is grounded used for connecting conducting equipment to ground. The power system model can have any number of grounds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GroundDisconnector
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A manually operated or motor operated mechanical switching device used for isolating a circuit or equipment from ground.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GroundingImpedance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A fixed impedance device used for grounding.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Junction
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A point where one or more conducting equipments are connected with zero resistance.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Line
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Contains equipment beyond a substation belonging to a power transmission line.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LinearShuntCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A linear shunt compensator has banks or sections with equal admittance values.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LoadBreakSwitch
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal operating conditions.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: MutualCoupling
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: This class represents the zero sequence line mutual coupling.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: NonlinearShuntCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A non linear shunt compensator has bank or section admittance values that differs.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: NonlinearShuntCompensatorPoint
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A non linear shunt compensator bank or section admittance value.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PetersenCoil
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A tunable impedance device normally used to offset line charging during single line faults in an ungrounded section of network.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PetersenCoilModeKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The mode of operation for a Petersen coil.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChanger
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A transformer phase shifting tap model that controls the phase angle difference across the power transformer and potentially the active power flow through the power transformer.  This phase tap model may also impact the voltage magnitude.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerAsymmetrical
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes the tap model for an asymmetrical phase shifting transformer in which the difference voltage vector adds to the primary side voltage. The angle between the primary side voltage and the difference voltage is named the winding connection angle. The phase shift depends on both the difference voltage magnitude and the winding connection angle.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerLinear
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Describes a tap changer with a linear relation between the tap step and the phase angle difference across the transformer. This is a mathematical model that is an approximation of a real phase tap changer.
The phase angle is computed as stepPhaseShitfIncrement times the tap position.
The secondary side voltage magnitude is the same as at the primary side.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerNonLinear
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The non-linear phase tap changer describes the non-linear behavior of a phase tap changer. This is a base class for the symmetrical and asymmetrical phase tap changer models. The details of these models can be found in the IEC 61970-301 document.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerSymmetrical
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes a symmetrical phase shifting transformer tap model in which the secondary side voltage magnitude is the same as at the primary side. The difference voltage magnitude is the base in an equal-sided triangle where the sides corresponds to the primary and secondary voltages. The phase angle difference corresponds to the top angle and can be expressed as twice the arctangent of half the total difference voltage.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerTable
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes a tabular curve for how the phase angle difference and impedance varies with the tap step.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerTablePoint
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes each tap step in the phase tap changer tabular curve.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PowerTransformer
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
An electrical device consisting of  two or more coupled windings, with or without a magnetic core, for introducing mutual coupling between electric circuits. Transformers can be used to control voltage and phase shift (active power flow).
A power transformer may be composed of separate transformer tanks that need not be identical.
A power transformer can be modeled with or without tanks and is intended for use in both balanced and unbalanced representations.   A power transformer typically has two terminals, but may have one (grounding), three or more terminals.
The inherited association ConductingEquipment.BaseVoltage should not be used.  The association from TransformerEnd to BaseVoltage should be used instead.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PowerTransformerEnd
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A PowerTransformerEnd is associated with each Terminal of a PowerTransformer.
The impedance values r, r0, x, and x0 of a PowerTransformerEnd represents a star equivalent as follows
1) for a two Terminal PowerTransformer the high voltage PowerTransformerEnd has non zero values on r, r0, x, and x0 while the low voltage PowerTransformerEnd has zero values for r, r0, x, and x0.
2) for a three Terminal PowerTransformer the three PowerTransformerEnds represents a star equivalent with each leg in the star represented by r, r0, x, and x0 values.
3) for a PowerTransformer with more than three Terminals the PowerTransformerEnd impedance values cannot be used. Instead use the TransformerMeshImpedance or split the transformer into multiple PowerTransformers.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: WindingConnection
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Winding connection type.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ProtectedSwitch
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A ProtectedSwitch is a switching device that can be operated by ProtectionEquipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RatioTapChanger
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A tap changer that changes the voltage ratio impacting the voltage magnitude but not the phase angle across the transformer.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: TransformerControlMode
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Control modes for a transformer.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RatioTapChangerTable
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes a curve for how the voltage magnitude and impedance varies with the tap step.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RatioTapChangerTablePoint
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes each tap step in the ratio tap changer tabular curve.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ReactiveCapabilityCurve
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Reactive power rating envelope versus the synchronous machine's active power, in both the generating and motoring modes. For each active power value there is a corresponding high and low reactive power limit  value. Typically there will be a separate curve for each coolant condition, such as hydrogen pressure.  The Y1 axis values represent reactive minimum and the Y2 axis values represent reactive maximum.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegulatingCondEq
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A type of conducting equipment that can regulate a quantity (i.e. voltage or flow) at a specific point in the network.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegulatingControl
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Specifies a set of equipment that works together to control a power system quantity such as voltage or flow. 
Remote bus voltage control is possible by specifying the controlled terminal located at some place remote from the controlling equipment.
In case multiple equipment, possibly of different types, control same terminal there must be only one RegulatingControl at that terminal. The most specific subtype of RegulatingControl shall be used in case such equipment participate in the control, e.g. TapChangerControl for tap changers.
For flow control  load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegulatingControlModeKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The kind of regulation model.   For example regulating voltage, reactive power, active power, etc.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegulationSchedule
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A pre-established pattern over time for a controlled variable, e.g., busbar voltage.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RotatingMachine
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A rotating machine which may be used as a generator or motor.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SeriesCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A Series Compensator is a series capacitor or reactor or an AC transmission line without charging susceptance.  It is a two terminal device.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ShortCircuitRotorKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Type of rotor, used by short circuit applications.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ShuntCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A shunt capacitor or reactor or switchable bank of shunt capacitors or reactors. A section of a shunt compensator is an individual capacitor or reactor.  A negative value for reactivePerSection indicates that the compensator is a reactor. ShuntCompensator is a single terminal device.  Ground is implied.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: VoltagePerReactivePower
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Voltage variation with reactive power.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: StaticVarCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A facility for providing variable and controllable shunt reactive power. The SVC typically consists of a stepdown transformer, filter, thyristor-controlled reactor, and thyristor-switched capacitor arms.

The SVC may operate in fixed MVar output mode or in voltage control mode. When in voltage control mode, the output of the SVC will be proportional to the deviation of voltage at the controlled bus from the voltage setpoint.  The SVC characteristic slope defines the proportion.  If the voltage at the controlled bus is equal to the voltage setpoint, the SVC MVar output is zero.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SVCControlMode
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Static VAr Compensator control mode.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Switch
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generic device designed to close, or open, or both, one or more electric circuits.  All switches are two terminal devices including grounding switches.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SwitchSchedule
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A schedule of switch positions.  If RegularTimePoint.value1 is 0, the switch is open.  If 1, the switch is closed.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SynchronousMachine
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electromechanical device that operates with shaft rotating synchronously with the network. It is a single machine operating either as a generator or synchronous condenser or pump.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SynchronousMachineKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Synchronous machine type.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: TapChanger
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Mechanism for changing transformer winding tap positions.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: TapChangerControl
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes behavior specific to tap changers, e.g. how the voltage at the end of a line varies with the load level and compensation of the voltage drop by tap adjustment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: TapSchedule
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A pre-established pattern over time for a tap step.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: TransformerEnd
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A conducting connection point of a power transformer. It corresponds to a physical transformer winding terminal.  In earlier CIM versions, the TransformerWinding class served a similar purpose, but this class is more flexible because it associates to terminal but is not a specialization of ConductingEquipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConformLoad
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: ConformLoad represent loads that follow a daily load change pattern where the pattern can be used to scale the load with a system load.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConformLoadGroup
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A group of loads conforming to an allocation pattern.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConformLoadSchedule
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A curve of load  versus time (X-axis) showing the active power values (Y1-axis) and reactive power (Y2-axis) for each unit of the period covered. This curve represents a typical pattern of load over the time period for a given day type and season.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DayType
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Group of similar days.   For example it could be used to represent weekdays, weekend, or holidays.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EnergyArea
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes an area having energy production or consumption.  Specializations are intended to support the load allocation function as typically required in energy management systems or planning studies to allocate hypothesized load levels to individual load points for power flow analysis.  Often the energy area can be linked to both measured and forecast load levels.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LoadArea
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The class is the root or first level in a hierarchical structure for grouping of loads for the purpose of load flow load scaling.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LoadGroup
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The class is the third level in a hierarchical structure for grouping of loads for the purpose of load flow load scaling.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LoadResponseCharacteristic
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Models the characteristic response of the load demand due to changes in system conditions such as voltage and frequency. This is not related to demand response.

If LoadResponseCharacteristic.exponentModel is True, the voltage exponents are specified and used as to calculate:

Active power component = Pnominal * (Voltage/cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage) ** cim:LoadResponseCharacteristic.pVoltageExponent

Reactive power component = Qnominal * (Voltage/cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage)** cim:LoadResponseCharacteristic.qVoltageExponent

Where  * means "multiply" and ** is "raised to power of".

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Quality61850.oscillatory
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: To prevent some overload of the communication it is sensible to detect and suppress oscillating (fast changing) binary inputs. If a signal changes in a defined time (tosc) twice in the same direction (from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0) then oscillation is detected and the detail quality identifier "oscillatory" is set. If it is detected a configured numbers of transient changes could be passed by. In this time the validity status "questionable" is set. If after this defined numbers of changes the signal is still in the oscillating state the value shall be set either to the opposite state of the previous stable value or to a defined default value. In this case the validity status "questionable" is reset and "invalid" is set as long as the signal is oscillating. If it is configured such that no transient changes should be passed by then the validity status "invalid" is set immediately in addition to the detail quality identifier "oscillatory" (used for status information only).

http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.comment: It represents the full model header and its contents is described by the Model class.

http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.label: Model
http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.comment:
A Model is a collection of data describing instances, objects or entities, real or computed. In the context of CIM the semantics of the data is defined by profiles. Hence a model can contain equipment data, power flow initial values, power flow results etc.
The Model class describes the header content that is the same for the FullModel and the DifferenceModel. A Model is identified by an rdf:about attribute. The rdf:about attribute uniquely describe the model data and not the CIMXML document. A new rdf:about identification is generated for created documents only when the model data has changed. A repeated creation of documents from unchanged model data shall have the same rdf:about identification as previous document generated from the same model data.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DateTime

A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.label: Model.DependentOn
http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.comment:
A reference to the model documents that the model described by this document depends on. In general there can be 0 or many Model.DependentOn depending on the profile and the content of the instance file.
For instance:
– A load flow solution depends on the topology model it was computed from
– A topology model computed by a topology processor depends on the network model it was computed from.
The referenced models are identified by the FullModel rdf:about attribute for full model documents and by DifferenceModel rdf:about attribute for difference model documents.
The references are maintained by the producer of the CIMXML document and the references are valid for the model with version and identifier for which the document was created.

http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.label: Model.Depending
http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.comment: All documents depending on the model described by this document. This role is not intended to be included in any document exchanging instance data.

http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.label: Model.Supersedes
http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.comment: When a model is updated the resulting model supersedes the models that were used as basis for the update. Hence this is a reference to the CIMXML documents which are superseded by this model. A model (or instance file) can supersede 1 or more models, e.g. a difference model or a full model supersede multiple models (difference or full). In this case more than one Model.Supersedes are included in the header. The referenced document(s) is (are) identified by the URN/MRID/UUID in the FullModel rdf:about attribute when full model(s) is (are) referenced and by the URN/MRID/UUID in the DifferenceModel rdf:about attribute when difference model(s) is (are) referenced.

http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDescri.label: Model.SupersededBy

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PositionPoint

Use a single position point instance to desribe a point-oriented location. Use a sequence of position points to describe a line-oriented object (physical location of non-point oriented objects like cables or lines), or area of an object (like a substation or a geographical zone - in this case, have first and last position point with the same values).

Power system resources can have measurements associated.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CoordinateSystem.crsUrn
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A Uniform Resource Name (URN) for the coordinate reference system (crs) used to define 'Location.PositionPoints'.
An example would be the European Petroleum Survey Group (EPSG) code for a coordinate reference system, defined in URN under the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) namespace as: urn:ogc:def:uom:EPSG::XXXX, where XXXX is an EPSG code (a full list of codes can be found at the EPSG Registry web site http://www.epsg-registry.org/). To define the coordinate system as being WGS84 (latitude, longitude) using an EPSG OGC, this attribute would be urn:ogc:def:uom:EPSG::4236.
A profile should limit this code to a set of allowed URNs agreed to by all sending and receiving parties.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: All power system resources at this location.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Location.PositionPoints
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Sequence of position points describing this location, expressed in coordinate system 'Location.CoordinateSystem'.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: String
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Date
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Date as "yyyy-mm-dd", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-dd(+/-)hh:mm".

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electrical connection point (AC or DC) to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Boolean
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConductingEquipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The parts of the AC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through terminals.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Equipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The parts of a power system that are physical devices, electronic or mechanical.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: IdentifiedObject
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: This is a root class to provide common identification for all classes needing identification and naming attributes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PowerSystemResource
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A power system resource can be an item of equipment such as a switch, an equipment container containing many individual items of equipment such as a substation, or an organisational entity such as sub-control area. Power system resources can have measurements associated.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Terminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An AC electrical connection point to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ControlArea
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A control area is a grouping of generating units and/or loads and a cutset of tie lines (as terminals) which may be used for a variety of purposes including automatic generation control, powerflow solution area interchange control specification, and input to load forecasting.   Note that any number of overlapping control area specifications can be superimposed on the physical model.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ActivePower
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Float
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: UnitSymbol
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The units defined for usage in the CIM.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: UnitMultiplier
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The unit multipliers defined for the CIM.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCConverter
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A unit with valves for three phases, together with unit control equipment, essential protective and switching devices, DC storage capacitors, phase reactors and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ReactivePower
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the quadrature component of the current.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Voltage
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Electrical voltage, can be both AC and DC.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCConverterDCTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A DC electrical connection point at the AC/DC converter. The AC/DC converter is electrically connected also to the AC side. The AC connection is inherited from the AC conducting equipment in the same way as any other AC equipment. The AC/DC converter DC terminal is separate from generic DC terminal to restrict the connection with the AC side to AC/DC converter and so that no other DC conducting equipment can be connected to the AC side.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CsConverter
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: DC side of the current source converter (CSC).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CsOperatingModeKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Operating mode for HVDC line operating as Current Source Converter.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CsPpccControlKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Active power control modes for HVDC line operating as Current Source Converter.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AngleDegrees
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Measurement of angle in degrees.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: CurrentFlow
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Electrical current with sign convention: positive flow is out of the conducting equipment into the connectivity node. Can be both AC and DC.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCBaseTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electrical connection point at a piece of DC conducting equipment. DC terminals are connected at one physical DC node that may have multiple DC terminals connected. A DC node is similar to an AC connectivity node. The model enforces that DC connections are distinct from AC connections.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: DCTerminal
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electrical connection point to generic DC conducting equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: VsConverter
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: DC side of the voltage source converter (VSC).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PU
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Per Unit - a positive or negative value referred to a defined base. Values typically range from -10 to +10.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Resistance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Resistance (real part of impedance).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: VsPpccControlKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Types applicable to the control of real power and/or DC voltage by voltage source converter.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PerCent
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Percentage on a defined base.   For example, specify as 100 to indicate at the defined base.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EquivalentEquipment
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The class represents equivalent objects that are the result of a network reduction. The class is the base for equivalent objects of different types.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EquivalentInjection
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: This class represents equivalent injections (generation or load).  Voltage regulation is allowed only at the point of connection.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A single or set of synchronous machines for converting mechanical power into alternating-current power. For example, individual machines within a set may be defined for scheduling purposes while a single control signal is derived for the set. In this case there would be a GeneratingUnit for each member of the set and an additional GeneratingUnit corresponding to the set.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Simple_Float
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: HydroGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generating unit whose prime mover is a hydraulic turbine (e.g., Francis, Pelton, Kaplan).

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: NuclearGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A nuclear generating unit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SolarGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A solar thermal generating unit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ThermalGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generating unit whose prime mover could be a steam turbine, combustion turbine, or diesel engine.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: WindGeneratingUnit
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A wind driven generating unit.  May be used to represent a single turbine or an aggregation.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AsynchronousMachine
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A rotating machine whose shaft rotates asynchronously with the electrical field.  Also known as an induction machine with no external connection to the rotor windings, e.g squirrel-cage induction machine.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: AsynchronousMachineKind
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Kind of Asynchronous Machine.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Breaker
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal circuit conditions and also making, carrying for a specified time, and breaking currents under specified abnormal circuit conditions e.g.  those of short circuit.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Disconnector
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A manually operated or motor operated mechanical switching device used for changing the connections in a circuit, or for isolating a circuit or equipment from a source of power. It is required to open or close circuits when negligible current is broken or made.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EnergyConsumer
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Generic user of energy - a  point of consumption on the power system model.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: EnergySource
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generic equivalent for an energy supplier on a transmission or distribution voltage level.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ExternalNetworkInjection
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: This class represents external network and it is used for IEC 60909 calculations.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Integer
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: GroundDisconnector
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A manually operated or motor operated mechanical switching device used for isolating a circuit or equipment from ground.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LoadBreakSwitch
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal operating conditions.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChanger
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A transformer phase shifting tap model that controls the phase angle difference across the power transformer and potentially the active power flow through the power transformer.  This phase tap model may also impact the voltage magnitude.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerAsymmetrical
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes the tap model for an asymmetrical phase shifting transformer in which the difference voltage vector adds to the primary side voltage. The angle between the primary side voltage and the difference voltage is named the winding connection angle. The phase shift depends on both the difference voltage magnitude and the winding connection angle.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerLinear
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Describes a tap changer with a linear relation between the tap step and the phase angle difference across the transformer. This is a mathematical model that is an approximation of a real phase tap changer.
The phase angle is computed as stepPhaseShitfIncrement times the tap position.
The secondary side voltage magnitude is the same as at the primary side.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerNonLinear
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The non-linear phase tap changer describes the non-linear behavior of a phase tap changer. This is a base class for the symmetrical and asymmetrical phase tap changer models. The details of these models can be found in the IEC 61970-301 document.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: PhaseTapChangerSymmetrical
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes a symmetrical phase shifting transformer tap model in which the secondary side voltage magnitude is the same as at the primary side. The difference voltage magnitude is the base in an equal-sided triangle where the sides corresponds to the primary and secondary voltages. The phase angle difference corresponds to the top angle and can be expressed as twice the arctangent of half the total difference voltage.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ProtectedSwitch
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A ProtectedSwitch is a switching device that can be operated by ProtectionEquipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RatioTapChanger
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A tap changer that changes the voltage ratio impacting the voltage magnitude but not the phase angle across the transformer.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegulatingCondEq
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A type of conducting equipment that can regulate a quantity (i.e. voltage or flow) at a specific point in the network.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RotatingMachine
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A rotating machine which may be used as a generator or motor.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: StaticVarCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
A facility for providing variable and controllable shunt reactive power. The SVC typically consists of a stepdown transformer, filter, thyristor-controlled reactor, and thyristor-switched capacitor arms.

The SVC may operate in fixed MVar output mode or in voltage control mode. When in voltage control mode, the output of the SVC will be proportional to the deviation of voltage at the controlled bus from the voltage setpoint.  The SVC characteristic slope defines the proportion.  If the voltage at the controlled bus is equal to the voltage setpoint, the SVC MVar output is zero.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: Switch
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A generic device designed to close, or open, or both, one or more electric circuits.  All switches are two terminal devices including grounding switches.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SynchronousMachine
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: An electromechanical device that operates with shaft rotating synchronously with the network. It is a single machine operating either as a generator or synchronous condenser or pump.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: SynchronousMachineOperatingMode
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Synchronous machine operating mode.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: TapChangerControl
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Describes behavior specific to tap changers, e.g. how the voltage at the end of a line varies with the load level and compensation of the voltage drop by tap adjustment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: LinearShuntCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A linear shunt compensator has banks or sections with equal admittance values.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: NonlinearShuntCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A non linear shunt compensator has bank or section admittance values that differs.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: RegulatingControl
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Specifies a set of equipment that works together to control a power system quantity such as voltage or flow. 
Remote bus voltage control is possible by specifying the controlled terminal located at some place remote from the controlling equipment.
In case multiple equipment, possibly of different types, control same terminal there must be only one RegulatingControl at that terminal. The most specific subtype of RegulatingControl shall be used in case such equipment participate in the control, e.g. TapChangerControl for tap changers.
For flow control  load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ShuntCompensator
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: A shunt capacitor or reactor or switchable bank of shunt capacitors or reactors. A section of a shunt compensator is an individual capacitor or reactor.  A negative value for reactivePerSection indicates that the compensator is a reactor. ShuntCompensator is a single terminal device.  Ground is implied.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: TapChanger
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Mechanism for changing transformer winding tap positions.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ConformLoad
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: ConformLoad represent loads that follow a daily load change pattern where the pattern can be used to scale the load with a system load.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: NonConformLoad
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: NonConformLoad represent loads that do not follow a daily load change pattern and changes are not correlated with the daily load change pattern.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: StationSupply
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Station supply with load derived from the station output.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCTerminal.connected
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
The connected status is related to a bus-branch model and the topological node to terminal relation.  True implies the terminal is connected to the related topological node and false implies it is not. 
In a bus-branch model, the connected status is used to tell if equipment is disconnected without having to change the connectivity described by the topological node to terminal relation. A valid case is that conducting equipment can be connected in one end and open in the other. In particular for an AC line segment, where the reactive line charging can be significant, this is a relevant case.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: The specified positive net interchange into the control area, i.e. positive sign means flow in to the area.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ControlArea.pTolerance
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Active power net interchange tolerance

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Active power at the point of common coupling. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for a steady state solution in the case a simplified power flow model is used.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment:
Reactive power at the point of common coupling. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for a steady state solution in the case a simplified power flow model is used.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCConverter.targetPpcc
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Real power injection target in AC grid, at point of common coupling.

http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.label: ACDCConverter.targetUdc
http://iec.ch/TC57/2013/CIM-schema-cim16.comment: Target value for DC voltage magnitude.

The ISO code is two characters country code as defined by ISO 3166 (http://www.iso.org/iso/country_codes). The length of the string is 2 characters maximum.
The attribute is a required for the Boundary Model Authority Set where this attribute is used only for the TopologicalNode in the Boundary Topology profile and ConnectivityNode in the Boundary Equipment profile.

messages.datatype: The datatype is not literal or it violates the xsd datatype.

http://entsoe.eu/CIM/SchemaExtension/3/1.label: TopologicalNode.fromEndName
http://entsoe.eu/CIM/SchemaExtension/3/1.comment:
The attribute is used for an exchange of a human readable name with length of the string 32 characters maximum. The attribute covers two cases:

	if the Boundary point is placed on a tie-line the attribute is used for exchange of the geographical name of the substation to which the “From” side of the tie-line is connected to.
	if the Boundary point is placed in a substation the attribute is used for exchange of the name of the element (e.g. PowerTransformer, ACLineSegment, Switch, etc) to which the “From” side of the Boundary point is connected to.

The attribute is required for the Boundary Model Authority Set where it is used only for the TopologicalNode in the Boundary Topology profile and ConnectivityNode in the Boundary Equipment profile.

messages.datatype: The datatype is not literal or it violates the xsd datatype.
